title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Measuring Cross-Lingual Policy Retention in Tool-Using Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.11110v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: When a tool-using agent is given the same task in a different language, does it still take the same steps? Multilingual evaluation rarely asks: it compares final answers and discards the actions. Yet those actions are the product: they fix cost and latency, decide how the system fails, and are the only auditable part of its behaviour. We make the action policy the measured object across 8 models, 6 parallel benchmarks and 41 languages (2.38M rollouts). The naive measurement fails: five confounds sit between raw trace similarity and any defensible claim, each able to flip a conclusion. Short traces score higher, empty traces score perfectly, unrelated traces agree by chance over half the time, the gap is capped by each model's reproducibility, and a model asked the same question twice in one language answers differently, leaving no baseline. We remove all five, and every correction makes the effect larger. Divergence proves structural

translated_title: 行动胜于言语：衡量工具使用智能体跨语言策略保持性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11110v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：当工具使用智能体在不同语言中被赋予相同任务时，它是否仍会采取相同的步骤？多语言评估很少提出这个问题：它比较最终答案并丢弃行动。然而，这些行动才是产品：它们决定成本和延迟，决定系统如何失败，并且是其行为中唯一可审计的部分。我们将行动策略作为测量对象，跨越8个模型、6个平行基准和41种语言（238万次执行）。朴素测量失败：原始轨迹相似性与任何可辩护的声明之间存在五个混淆因素，每个都能翻转结论。短轨迹得分更高，空轨迹得满分，不相关轨迹有超过一半时间偶然一致，差距受每个模型的可重复性限制，以及一个模型在同一语言中两次提问会给出不同答案，没有基线。我们消除了所有五个因素，每次修正都使效应更大。分歧被证明是结构性的。
tldr: 本文首次系统性地测量工具使用智能体在多语言任务中的行动策略一致性，通过消除五个关键混淆因素，揭示跨语言策略分歧是结构性的，而非测量误差。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically measures action-policy consistency in tool-using agents across languages for the first time, and by removing five key confounds, reveals that cross-lingual policy divergence is structural rather than a measurement artifact.
